display.title: Shabbos Chazon: A Glimpse of the Third Beis HaMikdash
display.summary_short: Why the Shabbos before Tisha B'Av is called Shabbos Chazon, and Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev's parable of a father who sewed three garments for his son.
display.summary_long: Rabbi Goldstein welcomes listeners back to Shema B'ni and thanks them for their letters. This coming Shabbos is special: we begin Devarim, the fifth book of the Chumash, and it is Shabbos Chazon, named for the haftorah 'Chazon Yeshayahu', which warns of what happens when the Jewish people forsake the Torah, a fitting theme for the Nine Days and for Tisha B'Av, which falls on Shabbos that year. Then comes a deeper reason. The third Beis HaMikdash is already built and waiting in Heaven, and our Torah, davening and mitzvos, especially Shabbos, can bring it down sooner. Rabbi Hillel of Paritch taught in the name of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev that on Shabbos Chazon Hashem shows every Jew a vision of it from afar. He compared it to a father who sewed a precious garment for his son, saw it torn, sewed a second that was torn too, and then locked the third away, showing it to the boy only at set times until he learned to take care of it. Children are encouraged to learn, daven, keep Shabbos and give tzedakah, so that they may feel something special this Shabbos.
display.lesson: Hashem has the third Beis HaMikdash ready and waiting; through Torah, davening, Shabbos and tzedakah we show we deserve it and bring it sooner.
